The dashboard stays on screen: leaving it or switching the tablet off requires the master code, or the access code if there is none (Back button, or long press in the top-left corner).
Home and Recent apps buttons, notification shade and power menu are blocked. The app is the home screen and starts with the tablet.
Android screen pinning: the system gesture can still unpin the app. In Android settings › Security › App pinning, enable \"Ask for PIN before unpinning\" to protect it.

For the full lock, make this app the device owner once, from a computer with the tablet connected over USB (USB debugging enabled). No account (Google, Samsung…) may be signed in on the tablet while running the command; accounts can be added back afterwards.
Choose this app as the home screen so it comes back with the Home button and when the tablet starts.

Folder as shown in Home Assistant › Media. With the file address (e.g. /local/media/Recordings), files are loaded directly; otherwise Home Assistant provides each address.
Windows share, Samba or NAS (SMB 2/3). Leave the user empty for guest access. Server may include a port (nas:445).
NFS v3. The export must accept non-privileged ports (\"insecure\" option, or \"Allow connections from non-privileged ports\" on Synology/QNAP). UID/GID: identity used to read the files.
Folder on the tablet (internal storage, SD card, USB drive…). Access is granted to this folder only.
Each camera uses an image or camera entity: its latest capture is shown while it is recent enough. No video.
No capture recognised: check the cameras and the file settings.
Home Assistant media do not provide the modification date.
Empty: date found automatically (20251104203012, 2025-11-04_20-30-12…). Otherwise a pattern such as yyyyMMdd_HHmmss (yyyy year, MM month, dd day, HH hour, mm minutes, ss seconds).
Ignored when pairing by name, e.g. \"_snap\" in cam1_20251104_snap.jpg. Automatic: same name, otherwise the video of the same camera starting just before the capture.
No camera: every file of the folder is shown, without a name.
Several cameras can share a folder: each one is recognised by a prefix or suffix of its files (extension excluded). \"Argus 1\" matches \"Argus 1_00_20251104203012.jpg\" but not \"Argus 10_…\".
image.* entity (the time of its latest image is used) or camera.*.

After a crash, the app reopens by itself. Android allows it when the app is device owner, the home screen, or allowed to display over other apps.

Checked every 12 hours, installed without confirmation (the app is device owner), then the app reopens.

At night, the screen goes black (or very dim) sooner; a touch or presence in front of the camera wakes it.

Doorbell, motion sensor…: the camera opens fullscreen when this entity is triggered, wakes the screen, then closes by itself. Not opened if the camera is protected by the code.

Your choice: home screen (simple, set on the tablet) or device owner (full).

Set on the tablet in a moment. The app comes back with the Home button and at startup; the kiosk uses screen pinning, which an Android gesture can remove (protect it with the tablet\'s PIN).
Without a computer: after a factory reset of the tablet, with a QR code.

1. Export the configuration (Settings › Dashboard › Export): the reset erases everything.
2. Take a photo of this QR code with a phone.
3. Reset the tablet from Android's settings.
4. On the welcome screen, tap the same spot 6 times, then scan the photo (connect to Wi-Fi if asked).
5. Android installs HA-MACS as device owner: import the configuration in the wizard.

http address outside the local network: the token and data travel unencrypted over the Internet. Use an https address.
Access over the Internet (Pangolin, Cloudflare Access…): headers sent with every request to Home Assistant.

Pangolin: create an access token (shareable link) on the Home Assistant resource, then paste its ID and value. Use an https address. If the proxy blocks signing in with the Home Assistant account, paste a long-lived token.
